findings.title: Org-filter searchKey does not capture the cached result's dependence on the organizationId
findings.body: The cache key is only realm+mode, and the searchKey is the organizationId. IdentityProviderListQuery stores one entry per searchKey. When an org changes membership of an IDP, only the three login keys are invalidated, which is fine. However, the query is built per search key and an IDP's enabled/org state may change via organization enable/disable or removal of an org, with no login invalidation. Org-bound IDPs are wrapped for isEnabled, but removing an org or unlinking an IDP through the organization provider can leave stale lists. getById invalidation of the IDP id does not invalidate the list query.

findings.title: Update invalidation relies on a possibly stale or null original model
findings.body: update() calls getById(model.getInternalId()), which may return the cached model. The login predicate is evaluated on that. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate calls getLoginPredicate on `original` and `updated`. The predicate reads idp.getConfig().get(...), which could NPE if the config is null. Also, if the model is returned wrapped, the enabled state reflects the organization's state, so the original's enabled state is misjudged (an org-disabled IDP looks disabled), which can skip a needed invalidation.

findings.title: remove() now fetches the IDP unconditionally and may NPE
findings.body: storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) can be null for a nonexistent alias. registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) is safe because the predicate checks nonNull, but the isInvalid branch still calls registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp), which throws an NPE on null (previous behavior was the same). The added DB query on every remove is also needless when the cache branch is taken.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate semantics changed without matching the search options
findings.body: The predicate now also requires org-linked IDPs to have BROKER_PUBLIC=true. getLoginSearchOptions is unchanged, and other callers of getLoginPredicate get new filtering behavior. Also, idp.getConfig() may be null, causing an NPE.

findings.title: Cleanup registered with the literal alias "alias"
findings.body: getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) uses the literal string "alias" instead of the created alias, so the IDPs are never cleaned up. This can leak state into other tests. The same bug appears for idp-alias-20.
